name: BattleStatusPanelVariants
summary: The four variants of the alternate battle unit status panel built by `Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt`. Each variant is a fixed tuple: the scene task that starts it, the four-word position block it passes, the ten-field number table it draws and the shared stat block that supplies the values. Modes 0 and 1 use the actor-side stat block and modes 2 and 3 the target-side block. Modes 0 and 3 are started alone; one battle presentation program starts modes 1 and 2 together.

members.name: mode 0
members.text: Started by `BattleTask_Slot13Entry`, which battle presentation programs 2, 3 and 6 run as their last task (slot 13, tag 17 in programs 2 and 3, tag 37 in program 6). First position word 0x008C. I: the A (first) actor-side panel.

members.name: mode 1
members.text: Started by `BattleTask_ActorForecastPanel` after the secondary-action preview has run and the predicted HP/MP have been copied into the UI manager; program 5 runs it in slot 12 with tag 19 beside mode 2. First position word 0x0089. I: the B (second) actor-side panel, the actor half of the forecast pair.

members.name: mode 2
members.text: Started by `BattleTask_TargetForecastPanel` after it swaps the two preview unit slots and refreshes twice; program 5 runs it in slot 13 with tag 18. First position word 0x0157. I: the B (second) target-side panel, the target half of the forecast pair.

members.name: mode 3
members.text: Started by `sub_140229D84`, a 78-byte wrapper that only refreshes the scene and seeds its own panel counter; program 4 runs it alone in slot 12 with tag 58. First position word 0x0151. I: the A (first) target-side panel.

behavior.text: the four position blocks are adjacent four-word blocks at 0x1408081E0, 0x1408081E8, 0x1408081F0 and 0x1408081F8. Only the first word differs (0x008C, 0x0089, 0x0157, 0x0151); word 1 is 0x00AA and words 2 and 3 are 0x0023 and 0x0034 in all four. Word 0/1 is the panel origin and word 2/3 extends the right and bottom edges of the frame.

the number tables are four 0x140-byte tables of ten 32-byte records with the inline names hp, hpmax, mp, mpmax, wt, wtmax, at, atmax, level and exp. The actor pair (0x140808200 and 0x140808480) points its value fields into the stat block at 0x1407832A0; the target pair (0x140808340 and 0x140808580) points into 0x140783320. Modes 0 and 1 draw identical numbers, as do modes 2 and 3.

the two stat blocks are scratch copies of a preview unit, refilled by `sub_140226E44` from the actor and target preview slots before each variant runs. Their word at +0x0A is read as a battle-unit-table slot (above 20 selects fallback constants), not a panel kind. Their +0x18 word is the unit byte +0x41 (or 100 when unit byte +0x1B8 is set), named wt in the number table; the panel body rewrites the +0x02 team code each frame and caps +0x18 at 100.

the first word of each position block is the panel's left edge: 0x008C and 0x0089 for the two actor panels, 0x0157 and 0x0151 for the two target panels. The four-word blocks are handed whole to the frame helper, so words 2/3 are used as width and height extensions, not as text ids.

mode 0 is the standing turn-status panel, mode 3 a lone target panel shown with the banner, and modes 1 and 2 the paired forecast panels (rests on the battle presentation programs that start them: 0 and 3 alone, 1 with 2). The A/B labels come from that pairing; the visible titles are not established.

a named record for the four position blocks and the two stat blocks; which program selects each variant; why modes 0 and 1 carry byte-identical number tables; the meaning of the 3 and 6 pixel difference between the two words inside each pair.

notes: Covers the four call sites, the four position blocks, the four number tables (all ten records each), the two stat blocks and the per-language cell tables, with `sub_140226E44` and `sub_140226CA0` for the stat-block fill. The four position blocks and the two stat blocks have no named global record; the page and this table name them by address. Addresses are build-specific.
open_questions: ? a record for the four position blocks and the two stat blocks; ? the visible titles of the four panels; ? what selects each battle presentation program; ? why the A and B tables of one role are duplicates.

behavior.text: the manager appends one agent per `Mem_Alloc` in this order; the vector index is the slot id (54 allocations and 54 appends).
the IDB comment on `UIAgentManager_CreateAgents` names slots 3 Startup, 5 Launcher, 6 Title, 19 Announce and 51 OpCredit; each one matches the class in that position.
eight slots are built by a named constructor (6, 11, 18, 19, 20, 37, 38, 48); the other 46 call the base agent constructor and store their vtable inline.
the 54 entries are contiguous and no vtable repeats; the manager constructor starts the vector empty, and every slot's object is allocated and constructed here.
the agent vector's allocator is at +8 and its begin, end and capacity at +16, +24 and +32; after the last append the dword at +176 is set to 1.
agents are read back by slot. `TavernMenu_OnCommand` reads the pointer at `begin + 88`, which is slot 11 (the Unit agent), and the System struct page records `begin + 37 * 8`.
the six agents with no FFTO prefix (Fade, Cursor, SoundVisualizer, NoticeDialog, Loading, Announce) are generic UI agents; the other 48 are FFTO screen agents.
the role lines are the class names read as plain descriptions; where the code was read further, the entry names it (Bar, Journal, Poach, Novel, EndSlate).
the role of UIAgentFFTOBattleContinuous beyond its name, and the meaning of the manager's +176 flag.

notes: This is a code table, not game content. Entries tagged I carry a role read from the class name; their vtable, constructor and size values are decoded from the allocation code. The class names are the vtables, the constructor addresses are the factories, and the size is the allocation. Every slot was read in `UIAgentManager_CreateAgents`; the eight named constructors were read separately to confirm the vtable each one stores. Agent fields are not described here.

name: UIAnimCurves
summary: The easing curves of UI keyframes: curve id to blend function of the position t within a key interval (UIAnim_Curve). A UIB file stores the interpolation id n; the game uses curve n + 1 (UIAnim_InterpToCurve), so the file id of a curve is its id minus 1. Every curve is single precision. pi is the float 3.1415927; b(t) is the bounce-out curve (id 32); Bez(x1, y1, x2, y2; t) is a cubic Bezier from (0, 0) to (1, 1) with control points (x1, y1), (x2, y2), solved for x = t (5 bisection steps, then a linear blend of the bracket).

members.name: Step
members.text: Also the result for id 0 and any id above 39.

members.name: Linear
members.text: Also the curve of any file id outside 0 to 35.

members.name: InSine
members.text: Second half of the glove's bob.

members.name: OutSine
members.text: First half of the glove's bob.

members.name: InOutBack
members.text: As coded (not the textbook in-out back).

members.name: InElastic
members.text: sub_140402C14; the in-out variants use it as e(t).

members.name: BezierA
members.text: Ids 34 to 39 are Bezier easings (sub_140402D38); t <= 0 gives 0 and t >= 1 gives 1.

members.name: BezierInOutAB
members.text: The last id UIAnim_InterpToCurve returns (file id 35).

members.name: BezierC
members.text: Ids 37 to 39 are in the evaluator but not reachable from a UIB file (UIAnim_InterpToCurve stops at 36).

behavior.text: UIB interpolation id n maps to curve n + 1 for n = 0 .. 35 and to curve 2 otherwise (UIAnim_InterpToCurve).
the Hand's Loop keys use file ids 19, 18 and 1: curves 20, 19 and 2.

members.text: Phase 0 calls SaveSlots_LoadFromFile(g_SaveManager) and sets the save-I/O word at qword_140D405B8+260 to 3; phase 1 waits until sub_1400C3790() returns 0 and then sets state 2.

members.text: No-op guard; state 1 sets it when the file load is idle.

behavior.text: the selector installed at +120 returns vtable slot 8 + state; states 0..2 use slots 8..10 (guard, sub_14018403C, guard).

the block has its own owner, handler and state fields; the agent update virtual does not advance it. I: only the agent state-2 handler advances it, by calling the handler at +112 each frame (that handler is not shown in the pseudocode read).

the selector has no bounds check, so a state 3 would read vtable slot 11, which is the same no-op guard used by agent state 0 (rests on the table layout read in the constructor; the table itself is not shown in the pseudocode).
no caller sets a dialog state above 2.

name: UISaveLoadStates
summary: The save/load agent's eleven states (ids 0..10). The state id lives in the agent's block A at +96; state n selects vtable slot 11 + n through the selector installed at +88. State 0 is the no-op resting state, states 1..4 bring the screen up, states 5..7 load, save and erase, state 8 picks a New Game + source, state 9 closes the screen and state 10 delays a target state behind a wait on another UI agent.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateIdle
members.text: No-op guard. The list screen rests here after state 4; events 0..3 are accepted only in this state.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateSavingOverlay
members.text: Enter: create and show the 80-byte UIAddonSaving overlay at +1584, load UI row 256, queue a new AUTOENHANCED autosave through sub_1400C480C, wait for the save queue and the overlay, then state 2.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateLoadSlotFile
members.text: Set dialog block state 1 (SaveSlots_LoadFromFile through sub_14018403C), run the dialog's phase 1, and go to state 3 when the dialog reaches state 2.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateBuildList
members.text: Allocate and attach the 1240-byte list add-on, store it at +1576. When mode bit 1 is set, request the five auto-slot summaries one per frame through sub_1400C4214(manager, n, 0) and copy each into descriptor n; then state 4.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateListEnter
members.text: Build the five auto entries from the descriptors at +256, select tab 0/1/2 from the mode bits, load UI row 252 and request the overlay hide. Phase 1 goes to state 0 when the hide finishes; phase 2 clears the mode bits.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateLoad
members.text: Load: phase 0 fades and either requests the slot's parts (+244 set) or calls SaveSlot_LoadToLive; phase 2 resumes the checkpoint or the scene and tears the screen down.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateSave
members.text: Save: phase 0 writes the selected manual slot from live with +140 as the situation; phase 1 waits for the file write and reloads the slot file; phase 2 refreshes the list and puts the cursor on the written slot.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateErase
members.text: Erase: phase 0 fills the slot record in the cache with 0xFF and marks the cache dirty; phase 1 waits for the write; phase 2 refreshes the list.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateNewGamePlus
members.text: New Game + pick: phase 0 clears focus, loads music track 8 in mode 2, fades to 26 and detaches the list; phase 1 writes the chosen slot to g_GlobalWork+128; phase 2 cleans up.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateClose
members.text: Close: phase 0 starts music track 7 (manual tab) or 8 (other tabs) in mode 1 and fades to 9; phase 1 waits for the fade and sets state 0; phase 2 clears the screen and cleans up.

members.name: UISaveLoad_StateDeferred
members.text: Deferred entry: while +232 is not 23, calls sub_1401D6DB0 with the UI base and the values at +232/+236; it enters +240 (5 for load or 8 for New Game +) when the helper returns 0. The pause callback sets +232 = 13 and +236 = 1; phase 2 resets +232/+236/+240.

behavior.text: the selector installed at +88 returns vtable slot 11 + state; states 0..10 therefore use slots 11..21, which hold the guard and the ten handlers listed here.

`UIAgent_SetState` runs the current handler with phase 2, stores the new state number, selects the new handler and runs it with phase 0. Phase 1 is delivered by the update virtual at vtable slot 1, which calls the handler at +80 with (agent, 1, the qword stored at g_Application+1160).
phase 0 receives a 0 third argument; phase 1 receives the qword stored at `g_Application+1160`. ?: the pseudocode shows only two arguments for the phase-2 call, so its third argument is not shown.
neither the old nor the new state number is passed to a handler; only the selector receives it.

in state 3, mode bit 1 gates the five-header collection. In state 4, bit 0 set selects tab 0; with bit 0 clear the tab is 1, and it is 2 when bit 2 is also set. State 4's exit clears bits 0..2. The in-game save opener `sub_140182DF8` sets bit 0 and stores its situation value at +140 before it enters state 1.

state 10's helper indexes the UI agent array at UI base + 296 with the value at +232 and compares the value at +236 minus 1 against a dword reached from that agent's +16 handle; what that dword means is ?.
state 0 is the resting state of the open list, resting on events 0..3 testing for it and on state 4 entering it.
no code sets an agent state above 10; the selector has no bounds check.

notes: The state blocks are the two 32-byte controls at +72 and +104. Only block A drives this registry; block B's states are the separate UISaveLoadDialogStates registry. The handler addresses are the ordinary vtable slots, not a second table. The overlay at +1584 is an 80-byte UIAddonSaving, created by state 1 and not a dialog. The storage fields are the agent struct's `state_a`, `state_a_handler` and `state_a_selector` (offsets +96, +80 and +88).
open_questions: ? no writer for state ids above 10; ? whether the +224 flag changes any state transition (only a clear was found).

name: UiScriptOpcodes
summary: The 29-slot handler table (image address 0x1406838F0) that UiScript_Run indexes with the opcode byte of each record; the conditional handlers also index it for the records they govern. Slot 8 is empty. The script ends at opcode 33 (0x21), which has no slot. Each handler takes the record pointer and returns the next record's pointer. Only slots verified in the table are listed.

name: UnitEventFlagBit
summary: The bits of the unit flag word at battle unit +504, which the battle build stores from the entry override row: one bit per flag byte (OverrideEntryData +0x8E..+0x97 and +0x99), plus bit 11 set by the equipment build.

members.name: special
members.text: Column special (+0x8E): the unit shows the 'Special' presentation (yellow panel background, 'ShowSpecial'); sub_14036099C reports side category 3 for it; its tile marker is kind 4 instead of 2.

members.name: flag_1
members.text: Column flag_1 (+0x8F): the unit's byte +401 is added to the list dword_1437A02D0 (sub_1401EE9B4) and sub_1401F5AFC treats the unit as valid. The reason is not known.

members.name: target_rescue
members.text: Column target_rescue (+0x90): the unit is an objective target while the active BattleObjective row has show_targets (BattleObjective_ShowsTarget): marker 'TargetRescue', panel state 'ShowRescue', and a stop of the objective camera tour.

members.name: target_attack

members.name: betrayal_panel

members.name: flag_8

members.name: flag_9

members.name: acts_first
members.text: Column acts_first (+0x99): Battle_TurnEngine phase 1 lets a unit with the bit act first once any unit has CT above 99; its CT is set to the highest CT and the bit is cleared.

members.name: equipment_flag
members.text: Not from the row: Unit_ApplyEquipment sets or clears it from the equipment attribute record's byte 25; Battle_AwardUnitJp and sub_14030C5A0 read it.

behavior.text: OverrideEntry_FillUnitEntry builds bits 0..10 in order from the flag bytes (each non-zero byte sets its bit); Battle_PlaceEntryUnits stores the word at unit +504.

notes: Behaviour: UnitEventFlagWord. The bit names are ours.
open_questions: ? the role of bits 1, 8 and 9 (bit 11's first reader sheets are not read here).

name: UnitIdentityIds
summary: A unit is identified by its marker (save record +0, the character template), not by its job (+2): the job changes, the marker stays. A story character's marker, its character-name row (+560, nxd.CharaName) and its own story job share one number; generic units share two markers (0x80, 0x81) and draw a name row at random.
